name: Fetch
text: I've reviewed the current link coverage and identified a batch of 200 unlinked elements that can be tackled next. To start, I propose running the `link-coverage-report.py` script on the `docs` repository to generate a list of unlinked elements, which will be saved to `unlinked-elements.csv`. I'll then use this list to create a new branch, `link-coverage-200`, where I'll begin adding links to the top 200 elements. My first command will be `git checkout -b link-coverage-200` to create the new branch.

name: Probe
text: I'm not convinced that running `link-coverage-report.py` is the most efficient approach, as it may not account for recently updated documentation that hasn't been reflected in the repository. Can Fetch provide evidence that this script is still effective and up-to-date, and that the output will be comprehensive enough to cover the next 200 unlinked elements? What metrics or benchmarks can we use to verify the accuracy of the generated `unlinked-elements.csv` file?
